claims.text: The seller delivery message (synthetic) asserts that all 10 service files were uploaded to the project folder and invites the buyer to check the delivery link.

citations.quote: [SIMULATED] Seller: I have uploaded all 10 service files to the project folder. Please check the delivery link.

claims.text: The buyer access complaint (synthetic) states the delivery link returned access denied and that the buyer could not open the service files.

citations.quote: [SIMULATED] Buyer: The delivery link says access denied. I cannot open the service files.

claims.text: The buyer partial-delivery report (synthetic) states the buyer could open the folder but only 4 of 10 agreed files were present, with 6 missing.

citations.quote: [SIMULATED] Buyer: I can now open the folder, but only 4 of the 10 agreed files are present. The other 6 are still missing.

claims.text: The seller follow-up (synthetic) acknowledges the buyer's message and says the seller will check folder permissions and the missing files.

citations.quote: [SIMULATED] Seller: Thank you for letting me know. I will check the folder permissions and the missing files.

contradictions.title: Seller says all 10 files delivered vs buyer says only 4 present
contradictions.detail: The seller's synthetic message asserts all 10 service files were uploaded, while the buyer's synthetic partial-delivery report says only 4 of 10 files are present and 6 remain missing. Partial delivery of 4 is not equivalent to delivery of all 10.

The two buyer statements differ on access, though both indicate the full deliverable was not accessible.

gaps.detail: Neither the seller's assertion nor the buyer's reports are independently verified in the provided material. The synthetic chat messages do not establish the state of the delivery folder or how many agreed files were actually accessible.

warnings: All chat deliverable messages (seller delivery, buyer complaints, seller follow-up) are explicitly marked [SIMULATED] synthetic material and must not be treated as verified real communications or proof of delivery.
The dispute snapshot is a sanitized historical sandbox reconstruction, not an original API response, not production data, and not a live fetch; it is not proof of the dispute's current status.
The snapshot records a capture status of COMPLETED; capture completion is not evidence that the buyer received the agreed service.
A seller assertion of delivery is not buyer acceptance; the buyer reports only partial receipt (4 of 10 files).
Importer assertion annotations (buyer_nonreceipt, partial_delivery, seller_delivery_claim) are unverified hints, not established facts.
No source defines the agreed deliverables, and the currency amount (USD 1.00) appears in the sandbox snapshot only; do not treat it as verified real value without review.
The initial empty dispute list followed by later appearance of the dispute reflects sandbox behavior and timing; it should not be interpreted as evidence about underlying conduct.
